title: Wildfire insurance payments and new smoke rules can advance before safe household recovery is visible
source_unit: California Department of Insurance wildfire claims tracker, State Farm claim investigation, and Smoke Damage Recovery Act announcement; aggregate claims, sampled regulatory review, and statewide legal response are separate units
geography: Los Angeles County Eaton and Palisades wildfire claims and California statewide insurance regulation

observations.period: Page rechecked September 29, 2026; underlying Eaton and Palisades claims tracker remains updated July 6, 2026

denominator.unit: reported claims across home, business, living-expense, auto, and other disaster-related claims

claim_payment_stage.value: partial payments and advance payments are visible; final adequacy, repair, and safe return are not

current_page_recheck.unit: official claims-tracker page recheck date; displayed figures unchanged from July 6 update

observations.method: California Department of Insurance claims tracker rechecked 2026-09-29; the page still displays its July 6, 2026 update and insurer-supplied aggregate claims and payment totals. Categories include multiple claim types and are not a unique-household or completed-recovery panel.
observations.uncertainty: The page remained unchanged at the recheck and says claims payments will grow as rebuilding progresses. It does not show claim-level payment adequacy, final settlement, repair completion, safe occupancy, renewal, or a stay/move outcome.
observations.subgroup: Eaton and Palisades fire-related claims across residential, commercial, living-expense, auto, and other disaster-related categories; the published aggregate does not identify household resources or property-level outcomes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Partial payment may be an appropriate interim step rather than an inadequate settlement, and aggregate dollars cannot establish either a recovery rate or a typical household experience.

observations.period: 2026; State Farm investigation and statewide smoke-damage rule

denominator.unit: State Farm claims reviewed in the Department's investigation sample

reported_problem_types.value: underpayment, delayed investigation, adjuster changes, smoke-damage disputes, and inadequate communication

smoke_damage_recovery_act.unit: statewide legal response establishing smoke-damage claim and inspection standards

household_recovery.unit: property-level safe repair, occupancy, and stable housing outcome

observations.method: California Department of Insurance investigation and official law announcement; the investigation sample, aggregate tracker, and statewide legal response are not pooled into one denominator.
observations.uncertainty: A regulatory sample is not a statewide violation rate. Enacting a standard does not establish compliance, contractor availability, payment, testing, remediation, or safe return at any property.
observations.subgroup: State Farm policyholders in the reviewed sample and California wildfire survivors covered by the new statewide smoke-damage framework; the records do not follow the same claim through the law's implementation.
observations.counterinterpretation: The investigation may identify serious problems in selected claims while many other claims proceed adequately; a new legal standard may improve future handling even before property-level outcomes are measurable.

related_sources.claim: California announced that AB 1795 was signed and described its smoke-damage presumption and inspection and claim-handling timelines.

boundary: This record establishes aggregate insurance payments, a sampled claim-handling investigation, and a statewide smoke-damage legal response. It does not establish a property-level payment rate, repair completion, safe occupancy, health result, renewed coverage, displacement, trust, or political action.
